name: @gjsify/gtk-runtime-win32-x64
description: Batteries-included GTK/GObject-Introspection runtime bundle for Windows x64 — lets @gjsify/node-gi load gi:// namespaces (GLib/GObject/Gio/cairo/Pango/Graphene/Gdk) with NO gvsbuild/system GTK. Platform-gated (win32/x64 only).

gaps.why: gst-plugins-good's mpg123 element links libmpg123, and the gvsbuild version this bundle is built from defines no project for that library — so it is not in the prefix and the element cannot be built. That is a different reason from "nobody asked": libvorbis IS a gvsbuild project and Ogg/Vorbis moved out of this list once the build named it, which is the whole difference between an omission and an absence. Measured on the published 0.48.0 bundle on Windows 11 with no gvsbuild on the host: `mpg123audiodec` resolves to NULL and `playbin3` never leaves READY for an mp3 while the same pipeline reaches PLAYING for a wav from the same ffmpeg run; a bundled mp3 fails as "missing a plug-in" and an mp3 stream as "Internal data stream error", which reads like a missing TLS backend and is not (#1544, #1626). Closing it needs a libmpg123 project in gvsbuild itself.

the gst-plugins-good element links libFLAC and gvsbuild defines no project for that library either — the same absence as MP3, read off the same project list, and neither is a licensing decision: libmpg123 is LGPL-2.1 and libFLAC is BSD-3-Clause. Measured in the same Windows 11 run against the published 0.48.0 bundle: `flacdec` resolves to NULL (#1626). Closing it needs a libFLAC project in gvsbuild itself.

the modern Windows sink, and the one absence here that costs no format: `directsound` ships and `autoaudiosink` resolves to it. Declared because it is the same silent absence, not because anything breaks.

`isomp4` demuxes the container and `audioparsers` supplies `aacparse`, after which the stream reaches no decoder at all. The two elements that would decode it are `faad` (gst-plugins-bad, GPL) and `avdec_aac` (libav, whose whole closure these bundles refuse), so shipping one is a redistribution decision for whoever ships the product rather than this bundle's.
